question.value: Is star formation in hosts of the most luminous z~2 quasars enhanced or suppressed (regulated), as judged from the intrinsic SFR distribution from ALMA 850um continuum?

evidence.quote: Here, we present ALMA observations to establish the intrinsic SFR-distribution of 20 luminous quasars at $z\sim2$, around the peak of AGN and SF activity.
Our sample of 20 luminous SDSS quasars was observed with ALMA during Cycle 5 (2017.1.00102.S; PI: A. Schulze) in May 2018 in Band 7.

findings_qualitative.value: SFR distribution of luminous z~2 quasars is consistent with the star-forming main sequence; no systematic enhancement or suppression.

evidence.quote: Thus, there is no evidence for a systematic enhancement or suppression (i.e., regulation or quenching) of star formation in the hosts of the most luminous quasars at $z\sim2$.

findings_qualitative.value: Only a weak relation between SFR and accretion rate.

evidence.quote: there is only a weak relation between SFR and accretion rate onto their supermassive black holes both for average and individual measurements.

claims.hypothesis: Star formation is regulated (quenched or enhanced) in hosts of the most luminous z~2 quasars
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 continuum of 20 quasars, AGN subtraction, MBB SFRs, log-normal fit, comparison with MS
claims.result: Log-normal SFR mean ~140 Msun/yr, dispersion 0.5 dex; consistent with MS
claims.finding: No evidence for systematic regulation of SF

evidence.quote: The SFR distribution is largely consistent with that of the star-forming MS.

claims.hypothesis: Models reproduce the SFR distribution of the most luminous quasars
claims.experiment: Compared with Hickox et al. phenomenological model and Magneticum simulation
claims.result: Observed mean ~0.4 dex lower and broader than Hickox; KS consistent with Magneticum
claims.finding: Consistent with Magneticum, not with Hickox model

evidence.quote: The SFR distribution is both broader and shifted to lower SFR than the simple phenomenological model by (cite: Hickox:2014), but consistent with results from a large scale cosmological hydrodynamical simulation

claims.experiment: Spearman and Kendall tests vs Lbol, MBH, lambda_Edd, CIV properties
claims.finding: Weak/no relation, though limited dynamic range

evidence.quote: We do not find any statistically significant correlation between SFR and AGN properties
